reference_independence.instrument: _jp2indep.mjs (reuses _jq20indep.mjs and _jq42indep.mjs unedited at their published hashes)
reference_independence.finding: THE CENT'S OBVERSE SET HAD NEVER BEEN CORRELATED. It is clean: raw NCC over all six obverse pairs runs -0.139..+0.219 against a 0.95 same-photograph line, backgrounds are uncorrelated (|NCC| <= 0.009) and the four illumination azimuths are -54.4 / 172.8 / 49.7 / -96.9 deg. Four independent observations. The same-photograph trap does NOT fire on this coin — the first set of five checked where it does not.
reference_independence.reverse: penny-rev.jpg vs penny-rev-2.png: raw 0.1028, design 0.5219 against a measured different-design floor of 0.3476 (+0.15 = 0.4976). Independent, but by a 0.024 margin, and the registration for that pair landed AT the translation bound, so 0.5219 is a LOWER BOUND, not a value.
reference_independence.caveat: 4 of 7 penny registrations landed at the +-0.03R translation bound (§4.1). Those design-NCC figures are lower bounds. Every INDEPENDENT verdict rests on raw NCC, which is bound-free.

dimensions.name: obverse silhouette

dimensions.caveat: penny-obv.md §2.3 reads this as 'the outline is the coin's shape, sized to +-1.0%'. This round adds evidence that the scale uncertainty is worse than that: _jp7edge.mjs measures where each reference's own silhouette lands in viewBox units, and penny-obv-2.jpg — THE FILE THE MASK WAS TRACED FROM — reads 45.71 against a definitional 47.00, with a p5..p95 spread of 9.4%. The measurement is bimodal on that file and is NOT a clean 2.8% claim, but it is a reason to re-derive the mask's scale before any future round leans on 0.954.

dimensions.name: structural rhythm
dimensions.justification: the Brenner obverse carries no repeated structural element of the kind §15.1 counts. Decided on the evidence, not assumed: _rvtarget.json holds no obverse entry for any coin, and the reference (penny-obv-3.jpg, read at 50px ladder) shows bust, hair, beard, coat and legend and no regular series. Lincoln's hair is a whorl of curls, not a directed or countable flow (penny-obv.md §7 says so and declined to run §12.4's strand tensor for the same reason). THE HAIR IS STILL A REAL UNMEASURED DEFICIENCY — it is D6's and D12's, not D4's.

dimensions.control: the NICKEL, both sides, same three tiers, rendered and read BEFORE the penny (_jp12-control.png). It shares bust(), coat(), struck(), reedGeom(), the field/ring pair and the specular arc with the cent. Chosen because round 0's priors are the judge's own — penny-obv.md's 'the hair is eight broad strokes', and my own arithmetic (Appendix R6).
dimensions.what_the_control_settled: the very wide pale rim annulus, the 26px solid-blob obverse and the pale specular sausage at ten o'clock are ALL present on the nickel. They are shared machinery, not cent defects — and the rim one is D5-rim, now measured.
dimensions.what_the_control_corrected: at 44px our colonnade reads as a comb of DARK teeth and I recorded that as an inverted tone polarity. At 380px the shafts are plainly PALE with dark intercolumniations, which is the coin's polarity. The 44px appearance is a tier-reduction artefact of shaft width, not a polarity error, and the note is kept as the record of the correction rather than deleted.

dimensions.name: device against field
dimensions.metric: mean/field and ink fraction over the disc interior, ours vs the photograph reduced to the SAME device pixel count
dimensions.locus: r < 40 viewBox units, ink = below 0.85 x own p90 field, tiers 26/44/84, no upsampling anywhere
dimensions.significance: THE WORST NUMBER ON THIS COIN. At the icon tier our obverse is 0.25 too dark against its own field — five times the gate — and carries 0.74 ink where the coin carries 0.34. D12 saw it independently: ours is a solid dark head-shaped blob on a pale disc, the coin is a soft mottle where the head is barely darker than the field. D3 passes on every internal relationship inside the head, which is exactly the blindness §3 says D13 exists to cover.
dimensions.instrument_note: _x6dark.mjs is REVERSE-ONLY (its PAIRS table pairs each id with a *-rev-* reference), so the obverse half of D13 has never been measured on any coin. _jp13d2d13.mjs computes the same quantity with the same frozen constants for both sides.

dimensions.name: device against field
dimensions.caveat: TWO INSTRUMENTS, TWO ANSWERS. `_x6dark.mjs` gives -0.0261 / -0.0210 / +0.0415 for the same three tiers where `_jp13d2d13.mjs` gives -0.0481 / -0.0066 / +0.0446. They differ in how the photograph is resampled (`_rvnorm.normalise` into a 512 grid vs a padded crop at the disc). The agreement is +-0.022, which is 44% of the gate. Both give PASS at all three tiers so the verdict is robust, but a future round that needs this number to 0.01 must settle which resampling is the frozen one.
dimensions.shape_finding: ink bbox ASPECT: ours 0.40 / 1.00 / 0.47 against the coin's 0.93 / 1.04 / 1.00 at 26 / 44 / 84 px. Our reverse ink is a wide flat band where the coin's fills a square, at two of the three tiers. mean/field passes and the SHAPE of the ink does not — the same class of miss as D5-band-reverse-bottom.
